subject: Shiny always crashes with 3.4.0 on Windows

messages.author: 3ef7a01c7d912ca2
messages.subject: Shiny always crashes with 3.4.0 on Windows
parts:
After I installed R 3.4.0 on Windows 64 bit, all attempts to start Shiny programs (including 01_hello) crash RStudio or Rgui and force total restart. All packages are current as of today, and all tested package re-builds work ok on my system.

The last words are:

Warning: body(fun) arguments is not a function.

I have tried with the version of Shiny from github with the same result.

Dieter

messages.author: 3ef7a01c7d912ca2
messages.subject: Re: Shiny always crashes with 3.4.0 on Windows
parts:
I reinstalled all packages, and problem is gone now. 

The warning: 

>>Warning in body(fun) : argument is not a function

is still there, but seems to be harmless.

messages.subject: Re: Shiny always crashes with 3.4.0 on Windows
parts:
We had installed everything as root.  Good news is we seem to have found the solution.  It seems that the release of the Just In Time (JIT) compiler as part of 3.4.0 was the culprit.  This seems to be the specific problem related to shiny apps:

https://www.r-statistics.com/2017/04/r-3-4-0-is-released-with-new-speed-upgrades-and-bug-fixes/
("For now, the compiler will not compile code containing explicit calls to browser(): this is to support single stepping from the browser() call.")

Adding the below line to the top of all of our app.R scripts has fixed (knock on wood) the problem.

enableJIT(0)

Thanks to our incredible Data Scientist, David Fackler for combing the release notes of 3.4.0 and putting together the pieces of the puzzle, and thanks to this group for all of the previous posts which helped us troubleshoot.  Hope this is helpful to others.

messages.subject: Re: Shiny always crashes with 3.4.0 on Windows
parts:
The only code blocks that were breaking (there were two) share a RMongo call as their unique element relative to other functions that worked fine:

dbGetQueryForKeys

I can't quite understand why/how this is a factor, but these were the only pieces that were breaking.  Both of these functions returned ggplots, so that is another candidate function, but my gut tells me it is related to RMongo.  We had no error messages to evaluate outside of "Segmentation Fault".

On Thursday, June 1, 2017 at 5:34:29 PM UTC-6, Joe Cheng [RStudio] wrote:
Wow, that's news to me! Do you have any idea what specific code in your Shiny app is triggering the segfault when jitting is on?

On Thu, Jun 1, 2017 at 9:32 AM Jesse Bell <bellj...@gmail.com> wrote:
We had installed everything as root.  Good news is we seem to have found the solution.  It seems that the release of the Just In Time (JIT) compiler as part of 3.4.0 was the culprit.  This seems to be the specific problem related to shiny apps:

https://www.r-statistics.com/2017/04/r-3-4-0-is-released-with-new-speed-upgrades-and-bug-fixes/
("For now, the compiler will not compile code containing explicit calls to browser(): this is to support single stepping from the browser() call.")

Adding the below line to the top of all of our app.R scripts has fixed (knock on wood) the problem.

enableJIT(0)

Thanks to our incredible Data Scientist, David Fackler for combing the release notes of 3.4.0 and putting together the pieces of the puzzle, and thanks to this group for all of the previous posts which helped us troubleshoot.  Hope this is helpful to others.
